podcast.title: Claimant in "Stairway to Heaven" Lawsuit
podcast.body: Randy California, the lead guitarist for Spirit, and later his estate after his death, claimed for years that Jimmy Page plagiarized Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for the iconic guitar arpeggio in Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." He sought a share of the estimated $500 million net worth of "Stairway to Heaven" through a contentious lawsuit that went all the way to the Supreme Court in 2020 before being ultimately dismissed. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."

xref.title: Accused of Plagiarism for "Stairway to Heaven"
xref.body: Jimmy Page, guitarist for Led Zeppelin, was accused by Randy California of Spirit (and his estate) of ripping off the guitar arpeggio from Spirit's instrumental "Taurus" for Led Zeppelin's "Stairway to Heaven." This led to a contentious, years-long court battle that concluded at the Supreme Court in 2020, with the court ultimately rejecting the plagiarism claim. "For years, Randy California, lead guy at Spirits, and then his estate after he died, claimed that Jimmy Page ripped off Taras for Stairway to Heaven."
